## Declarations and implementations

```plato

//==
// # Polyhedral solids
//
// The flat-faced convex solids named by their symmetry rather than by a
// generator: right regular prisms, pyramids, and antiprisms, plus the five
// Platonic and thirteen Archimedean solids
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyhedron). Each is centered at its frame
// origin in the frame's orientation. The parametric boundary surfaces of the
// prism and pyramid families live in `solids.library.plato`.

//==
// # Polyhedral solids

// A right regular prism: two parallel regular SideCount-gons of circumscribed
// radius Radius in planes perpendicular to the frame's Z axis, separated by
// Height and joined by rectangles (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prism_(geometry)).
// (The general polygon-swept prism is Prism3D, `polygons.types.plato`.)
type RegularPrism
    implements IConvexSolid, IParametricSurface, IPolygonMesh3D
{
    Frame: Frame3D;
    SideCount: Integer;
    Radius: Number;
    Height: Number;
}

// A right regular pyramid: a regular SideCount-gon of circumscribed radius
// Radius in the plane perpendicular to the frame's Z axis at -Height/2,
// tapering to an apex on that axis at +Height/2
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyramid_(geometry)). (The general polygon-based
// pyramid is Pyramid3D, polygons.plato.)
type RegularPyramid
    implements IConvexSolid, IParametricSurface, IPolygonMesh3D
{
    Frame: Frame3D;
    SideCount: Integer;
    Radius: Number;
    Height: Number;
}

// A right pyramid on an axis-aligned square base of side BaseLength, centered
// on the frame's Z axis at -Height/2, tapering to an apex at +Height/2. The
// square-base special case kept separate from RegularPyramid because its base
// is axis-aligned rather than inscribed in the unit circle
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Square_pyramid).
type SquarePyramid
    implements IConvexSolid, IParametricSurface, IPolygonMesh3D
{
    Frame: Frame3D;
    BaseLength: Number;
    Height: Number;
}

// A right antiprism: two parallel regular SideCount-gons rotated a half step
// against each other and joined by a band of 2 * SideCount triangles
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiprism).
type Antiprism
    implements IConvexSolid, IPolygonMesh3D
{
    Frame: Frame3D;
    SideCount: Integer;
    Radius: Number;
    Height: Number;
}

// One of the five Platonic solids (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platonic_solid),
// each naming the unit solid: centered at the origin, axis-aligned, with
// vertices at circumscribed radius one. `PolygonMesh3D(PlatonicSolid)` in
// `solids.library.plato` is the mesh; place it by transforming that mesh.
type PlatonicSolid
    = Tetrahedron | Cube | Octahedron | Dodecahedron | Icosahedron;

// One of the thirteen Archimedean solids
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archimedean_solid), each naming the unit
// solid at circumscribed radius one.
type ArchimedeanSolid
    = TruncatedTetrahedron
    | Cuboctahedron
    | TruncatedCube
    | TruncatedOctahedron
    | Rhombicuboctahedron
    | TruncatedCuboctahedron
    | SnubCube
    | Icosidodecahedron
    | TruncatedDodecahedron
    | TruncatedIcosahedron
    | Rhombicosidodecahedron
    | TruncatedIcosidodecahedron
    | SnubDodecahedron;

// One of the thirteen Catalan solids (duals of the Archimedean solids)
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalan_solid). All faces of a given solid
// are congruent (face-transitive); they do not mix polygon sizes. Initial
// hybrid construction lives in C# `Ara3D.Geometry.Polyhedra` /
// `ConwayOperators` (Platonic seeds + dual/ambo/truncate aliases). Each names
// the unit solid at circumscribed radius one.
type CatalanSolid
    = TriakisTetrahedron
    | RhombicDodecahedron
    | TriakisOctahedron
    | TetrakisHexahedron
    | DeltoidalIcositetrahedron
    | DisdyakisDodecahedron
    | PentagonalIcositetrahedron
    | RhombicTriacontahedron
    | TriakisIcosahedron
    | PentakisDodecahedron
    | DeltoidalHexecontahedron
    | DisdyakisTriacontahedron
    | PentagonalHexecontahedron;
```
